gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-anuphan: Classic lettering from Edo SZ, every stroke one constant width, makes the bold statement up top. And Anuphan does the gentler talking, with big round bowls and open curves that leave clear gaps.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-arimo: Cultural weight comes through in Edo SZ, whose lowercase carries the stature of cast iron capitals in one constant stroke. Arimo does the opposite job, a tall mean line and spacious gaps in its rounded glyphs.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-athiti: Sturdy and storied up top: Edo SZ gives its lowercase cast-iron stature with a single constant stroke. Athiti, a friendly sans-serif, leaves a see-through gap in each s.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-fresca: Cast-iron stature, lowercase and all: Edo SZ holds a constant stroke from start to finish. Fresca does the quieter job, with no calligraphic thinning and short ascenders above big bowls.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-heebo: Stately and stout: Edo SZ never thins its horizontals. Heebo's tall central band of text and curves that stop short of closing should make a sans-serif body glide down the page.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-huninn: Sturdy cultural lettering: Edo SZ holds one constant stroke width. Huninn is the modern counterpart, its lowercase rising close to cap height while crossbars stay fat as the stems they join.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-inter-tight: Inter Tight draws lines like bent tubing, with short ascenders barely poking above the lowercase. Inter Tight carries the reading forward at a brisk pace, a modern foil to the cast-iron lowercase of Edo SZ.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-kedebideri: Edo SZ gives every glyph an unmodulated line, with lowercase that has the stature of cast iron capitals. But it earns its keep big and brief, while Kedebideri, a rounded sans, stays open and inviting.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-lexend-deca: Lexend Deca reads approachable and clean, its unshaded line never swelling and its terminals stopping short of curling back in. Next to it, Edo SZ feels classic and cultural, like cast iron.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-liter: Lowercase with the stature of cast iron capitals gives Edo SZ its classic, cultural presence, all in one constant stroke. Liter takes the modern side, with no stroke contrast and wide mouths on its round forms.
